newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed up on Wednesday, boosted by a recovery in other markets and as the Treasury's monthly refunding came to an end, dealers said.
But volume was relatively low and traders remained wary.
"Even though we'll see the market rising tomorrow, we know that the market's underlying tone has changed. Soon it'll take a trip underground," a dealer in Madrid said.
But on Wednesday, Spain outperformed other European markets, with the 10-year cash spread over Bunds down to 125 basis points from 135 bps at the close on Tuesday.

Despite a relatively strong peseta, which was trading late on Wednesday at around 84.65/67 per mark, the gloomy outlook suggested a cautious approach by the Bank of Spain at its regular repurchase auction on Thursday, dealers said.
A Reuter poll showed no analysts expected a change in the key money market rate at the repurchase operation.
Spain's money market rate stands at 5.75 percent.
